summary: Backend-only end-to-end verification of AMASS Agent Ecosystem Phase 1 (/app/backend/agent_platform.py). 30 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_agent_platform_phase1.py against https://property-os-africa.preview.emergentagent.com/api. RESULT: 28/30 PASSED, 2 FAILED. Real bug found: POST /api/agent-platform/subscription/activate returns HTTP 500 (ObjectId not JSON serialisable) because _finalize_subscription returns the freshly-inserted sub_doc which motor has mutated to include the raw MongoDB _id. The database side-effects (subscription insert, founding counter increment, pending doc deletion, notification insert) all complete correctly before the response serialisation fails — verified via /subscription/me returning the new Pro sub, /founding counter incrementing (baseline 0 → 2 across two test runs), and quota reflecting Pro (limit=30). Everything else works: plans catalog shapes/values (Starter 0/5, Pro 15000/10000/30 founding-price on, Agency 50000/35000/150), founding counter (target 500, is_open true), subscribe/starter immediate activation, subscribe/pro returns pending_reference agentsub_..., founding counter increments after activate (verified out-of-band due to 500), /subscription/me reflects Pro with listing_limit 30, /subscription/cancel drops back to Starter, quota returns at_limit true with 9 active vs 5 starter limit, POST /api/properties returns exact 402 payload {error:'plan_limit_reached', plan_id:'starter', limit:5, active:9, ...} on Starter, POST succeeds on Pro. Onboarding returns 5 steps (account/professional/kyc/plan/listings) with percent + can_go_live + starter_kit_status. Starter-kit/me returns {status,user_id,kit_type}. All admin routes (list agents with status/plan/q filters, verify agent → approved, suspend/unsuspend → suspended/approved, PATCH /admin/plans/pro then revert, starter-kits status processing→dispatched→delivered, /admin/agents/kpis full shape) return 200 for demo (in ADMIN_EMAILS). All 6 admin routes return 403 for a fresh non-admin. Regression sweep green on /auth/login, /auth/me, /properties, /marketplace, /wallet/dual, /earn/tasks, /agent/promotions/config, /improve/catalog, /payments/initialize (mocked). The second reported test failure (test_founding_counter_incremented KeyError) is a pytest-xdist worker-isolation artefact — the STATE dict is per-worker and TestPlansCatalog ran on gw1 while TestSubscribeFlow ran on gw0, so the baseline never crossed workers. The underlying feature works — counter went from 0 to 2 (once per activate call, both across two runs) confirmed via curl.

critical.issue: Returns HTTP 500 with 'ObjectId is not iterable' TypeError. Root cause: agent_platform.py:614 returns {'ok': True, 'subscription': sub_doc} where sub_doc was just passed to `await db.agent_subscriptions.insert_one(sub_doc)` on line 589 — motor mutates the input dict to add the raw ObjectId _id, and FastAPI's jsonable_encoder chokes on it. Server-side side-effects (subscription persisted, founding counter incremented, pending cleared, notification created) all complete correctly before the response fails — verified via /subscription/me returning Pro with listing_limit=30, /founding claimed rising to 2, and /quota reporting plan_id=pro. Fix: either pop '_id' before returning (`sub_doc.pop('_id', None)`) or re-fetch with projection like `await db.agent_subscriptions.find_one({'id': sub_doc['id']}, {'_id': 0})`. Same pattern applies to _finalize_subscription's early-return on line 561 where `already` is fetched WITH {'_id':0} — good — but the later insert path skips that projection. Reference: /app/backend/agent_platform.py:589-614.

action_items: Fix HTTP 500 on POST /api/agent-platform/subscription/activate — strip MongoDB _id from the returned sub_doc in _finalize_subscription (/app/backend/agent_platform.py:614). Suggested one-liner: `sub_doc.pop('_id', None)` immediately after the insert_one, or return via `await db.agent_subscriptions.find_one({'id': sub_doc['id']}, {'_id': 0})`.

Same pattern likely lurks in the future Paystack/Flutterwave webhook path that will call the exposed router._finalize_subscription — because that wrapper returns the same sub_doc, any webhook handler that serialises the return value will also 500. Fix once in _finalize_subscription itself.

Optional: also strip _id from the notification-insert / pending-insert docs that flow through _finalize_subscription — pending_agent_subscriptions.insert_one on line 508 mutates the dict, but only reference is echoed, so it's currently latent.

No other action items required — all other Phase 1 features (plans catalog, quota enforcement 402 payload, subscription cancel, onboarding, starter-kit workflow, admin CRUD, KPIs, non-admin 403, founding counter) verified end-to-end and passing.
critical_code_review_comments: MongoDB _id leak in agent_platform.py:589-614 — see critical bug above. This is exactly the class of issue called out in the code-review guidelines ('Always exclude mongodb objectId _id').

agent_platform.py:_finalize_subscription is exposed on the router object as `router._finalize_subscription = _finalize_subscription` (line 617). This is fine for internal wiring but couples the payments webhook to a private-looking attribute — consider extracting to a module-level function receiving `db` so the webhook can import it cleanly without touching a router attribute.

agent_platform.py:_founding_counter increment happens inside _finalize_subscription only when pending.get('is_founding_price') is true (line 592). If an admin lowers pro's monthly_price_ngn below founding_price_ngn, the `use_founding` computation on line 471 becomes false and no counter increment fires — behaviour is correct but subtle; worth a comment.

agent_platform.py:check_listing_quota (line 334) counts ALL non-archived properties as active, including status='coming_soon' which is what freshly-created listings default to (server.py:643). Confirmed via test: demo has 9 active on Starter (limit 5) so 402 fires — good. But once starter listings become 'sold' or 'rented' they'll still count until archived. Consider excluding terminal statuses.

agent_platform.py:list_plans (line 421-429) reads the seeded DB docs but the response body relies on _plan_to_public which reads defaults from DEFAULT_PLANS via .get(...) fallbacks — an admin who PATCHes a plan to REMOVE a field (e.g. sets listing_limit to null) would end up with the default because we don't distinguish None from unset. Pydantic on AdminPlanUpdateIn already filters None (line 864) so this is defensive-only.

agent_platform.py:cancel_subscription (line 619) inserts a synthetic starter subscription every time cancel is called. If a user cancels twice they'll end up with two active starter subs. Fix: either update-existing-or-insert, or add a unique index on (user_id, status='active') to prevent this. Currently harmless because _active_subscription just returns find_one, but count/plan-distribution KPI queries will double-count.

rca_of_issue: Bug: POST /api/agent-platform/subscription/activate → 500. Reproduction: (1) login demo, (2) POST /api/agent-platform/subscription/subscribe {plan_id:'pro'} → get pending_reference, (3) POST /api/agent-platform/subscription/activate?pending_reference=<ref> → 500 with FastAPI ValueError chain rooted at 'ObjectId object is not iterable'. Backend log excerpt: File '/root/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/fastapi/encoders.py', line 322, in jsonable_encoder → data = dict(obj) → TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable. Cause: agent_platform.py:589 does `await db.agent_subscriptions.insert_one(sub_doc)` — motor mutates sub_doc adding raw BSON _id — then line 614 returns `{'subscription': sub_doc}` — FastAPI's jsonable_encoder recurses into sub_doc and hits the ObjectId which has no __dict__ and isn't iterable → 500. All DB side-effects complete before the crash: subscription persisted, founding counter incremented ($inc:{claimed:1}), pending cleared, notification inserted — verified via /subscription/me returning the new Pro sub and /founding counter reading 2 after two failed activates. Mitigation: pop '_id' before returning OR re-fetch with projection {'_id':0}. Same file already does the correct pattern in the `already` branch on line 557 — apply consistently.
